narrative.overview: The site should feel like the technician who shows up on time, looks at the actual equipment and explains the problem straight: calm, competent, unhurried, nothing to sell. This records the system as built on 2026-11-24; direction confirmed with Dennis is evolve, don't replace: lime and the logo stay, fonts, background and layout may change.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white (cream) page, near-black ink, one lime accent.
Serif display headings (Playfair Display) over light sans body text (Inter 300).
Fully rounded pill buttons; softly rounded cards and fields.
Flat surfaces with hairline borders; shadows only on the fixed nav when scrolled and on floating elements.
Mobile-first booking flow with time slots shown directly in the form.

rules.name: The Lime Is a Fill Rule
rules.body: Lime carries buttons, marks and dark-background text. Never set lime text on cream, paper or white.

rules.name: The Readable Floor Rule
rules.body: No text the homeowner must read goes below 14px (0.875rem), and body copy uses weight 400 or more on light backgrounds.

dos: Do keep Field Lime (#8DC63F) and the Solar Review logo in any evolution.
Do use lime as a fill or on dark backgrounds, with ink text on lime fills.
Do keep one clear primary action per section: book the free evaluation, with the phone number as fallback.
Do keep the booking form and time slots together on /book.
donts: Don't set lime text on cream, paper or white.
Don't put readable text below 14px or use weight 300 for body copy on light backgrounds.
Don't add an uppercase eyebrow label above every heading.
Don't add glows, side-bar accent stripes or decorative gradients.
Don't use customer job photos, invented testimonials or invented statistics as decoration.
